Confusable pairs among roundabout, ramp, traffic stop, deer and procession rules, where the right action depends on where you are or what you see; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A01
Before entering a roundabout you yield to pedestrians, bicycles, semitrucks and the traffic on your left that is already circulating. [A01]
Why it matters: group roundabouts; confusable who to yield to.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A01
A safe gap is needed to enter a busy roundabout, but an empty roundabout may be entered without stopping. [A01]
Why it matters: group roundabouts; misconception always stop before entering.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A01
Outside the roundabout you pull over for an emergency vehicle, but inside it you first exit at the next right and only then pull over. [A01]
Why it matters: group emergency vehicles; confusable before versus after entering.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A01
The signal used to leave a roundabout is the right turn signal, given as you reach your exit. [A01]
Why it matters: group roundabouts; misconception signal left to exit.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A02
A pedestrian at the curb looks left for oncoming traffic, while a pedestrian on the crosswalk island looks right. [A02]
Why it matters: group roundabout pedestrians; confusable curb versus island.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A03
At a two-lane roundabout, use the left lane for left turns or U-turns, use the right lane for right turns, and follow the pavement markings, arrows, or signs to go straight [A03].
Why it matters: group roundabout lanes; confusable general rule versus two-lane layout; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A03
At a two-lane roundabout you yield to traffic in both circulating lanes, not just the lane nearest you. [A03]
Why it matters: group roundabouts; misconception yield only to the outer lane.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A03
Ramp meters operate only while the Ramp Metered When Flashing sign is lit, and then each lane waits for its own green. [A03]
Why it matters: group ramp meters; confusable metered versus not metered.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A03
At a ramp meter you pull all the way up to the white stop line because that is where your tires trigger the pavement sensors. [A03]
Why it matters: group ramp meters; misconception stop anywhere on the ramp.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A04
A diverging diamond interchange is meant to improve safety, reduce crowding and lower the cost of new roads, and drivers get through it by following its signs, signals and markings. [A04]
Why it matters: group interchanges; prereq signals and markings.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-R11 | anchor: A05
At a traffic stop you stay in the vehicle with your seat belt on, rather than getting out to meet the officer. [A05]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; misconception step out of the car.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-R12 | anchor: A05
A ticket is contested before a judge or court, not by arguing with the officer at the roadside. [A05]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; confusable roadside versus court.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-R13 | anchor: A05
Seeing a deer's eyes calls for slowing down and using the horn, and you keep watching because more deer may follow. [A05]
Why it matters: group deer; misconception one deer means the danger has passed.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-R14 | anchor: A05
The police issue the tag for a deer you hit, and you still call them to report its location even if you do not keep it. [A05]
Why it matters: group deer; confusable keeping versus leaving the deer.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-R15 | anchor: A05
In a funeral procession the lead vehicle must follow traffic signs and signals, and every vehicle in the line keeps its headlights on. [A05]
Why it matters: group processions; confusable lead vehicle versus line vehicles.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0047]
